newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta to open more casinos, cut entry age to 18.
newsitem.headline: Malta to open more casinos, cut entry age to 18.

text.p: Malta is planning to open two or three casinos in luxury hotels and let 18-year-olds frequent them in a bid to increase tourism.
The Mediterranean island has only one casino, run by a state-owned company, Casma Ltd, and the present minimum age for going into the casino is 25 years.

The government on Monday issued a white paper under which Tourism Minister Karmenu Vella said it intended to award a 10-year licence to Casma, with provisions that would allow it to select other operators to run casinos in two or three five-star hotels.
"The purpose of the changes is to improve casino facilities, attract more tourists, generate employment and increase national revenue," Vella said, adding that the minimum age of entry would be 18.
But the minister said that in an effort to reduce the dangers of gambling for the Maltese, casino advertising in areas not frequented by tourists would be banned.
